description: Gold evaluation set for PolicyLens. Each item defines a question, the expected system behaviour, and (where applicable) the correct source document(s). expected_behavior is one of: answer, clarify, refuse.

items.question: What is our refund policy for enterprise customers in Germany?
items.notes: Must use the CURRENT version, not the superseded v1. This is the flagship example question from the PRD.

items.question: How many days do enterprise customers in Germany have to request a refund?
items.notes: Correct answer is 14 days (current). A system pulling the superseded doc would incorrectly say 30 days.

items.question: What was the refund window for German enterprise customers before the 2025 policy change?
items.notes: Explicit historical question — correct behaviour is to reference the superseded doc, since it's what's being asked about. Tests that the system doesn't refuse superseded content outright, only prefers current content by default.

items.question: Do SMB customers in Germany get a statutory withdrawal right on refunds?
What is the refund policy for enterprise customers in the US?
Can an SMB customer in the US get a refund on an annual plan?
What is the cancellation window for a UK SMB customer under consumer regulations?
What is the refund policy for enterprise customers in the UK?
items.notes: Deliberate gap — no UK enterprise refund document exists. System must not fabricate an answer by borrowing from UK SMB or DE enterprise docs.

items.question: What is our refund policy?
items.notes: No jurisdiction or segment given, and refund policy genuinely varies by both. Correct behaviour is to ask for jurisdiction/segment, or explicitly state the answer depends on both and summarise the variants — NOT to silently pick one.

items.question: How long do customers have to cancel and get their money back?
items.notes: Same ambiguity as q009, phrased differently, to test robustness of the ambiguity detector rather than keyword matching on 'refund policy'.

items.question: How long do we retain customer account data in the US after account closure?
items.notes: Must use current (3 years), not superseded (7 years).

items.question: Is support ticket data in the US kept indefinitely?
items.notes: Correct answer is no (24 months) under current policy; the superseded policy said indefinitely. Tests whether the system surfaces the superseded claim by mistake.

items.question: How long must we keep financial records under German law?
What's the retention period for financial records under UK rules?
What is our data retention policy in France?
items.notes: France is not a jurisdiction covered anywhere in the corpus. Tests whether the system incorrectly generalises from DE/EU GDPR content to 'answer for France too'.

items.question: How many days of paid annual leave do full-time employees get in Germany?
How much PTO do German contractors get?
items.notes: Deliberate gap — no DE contractor PTO document exists. System should explain contractors are governed by individual agreements, not fabricate a day count by analogy to full-time policy.

items.question: What is the PTO policy for contractors in the US?
items.notes: Deliberate gap.

items.question: How much PTO do full-time employees get in the US?
How many days of annual leave do UK full-time employees get?
items.notes: Must use current (27 days), not superseded (25 days).

items.question: How many days of unused UK annual leave can be carried into the next year?
items.notes: Current carry-over is 10 days, superseded was 5 days.

items.question: How is holiday pay handled for UK contractors working through an umbrella company?
How long do I have to submit an expense claim in Germany?
What receipt is required for expense claims over $0 under the US accountable plan rules, and what's the submission deadline?
Can I mail paper receipts to Finance for a UK expense claim?
items.notes: Current policy no longer accepts mailed paper receipts (digital app submission only); superseded policy required mailing them. Tests whether the system flags the practice as discontinued rather than confirming it's allowed.

items.question: What's the threshold above which a UK expense claim needs manager approval?
How should a data subject access request from a German individual be submitted?
items.notes: Current process requires the Privacy Request Portal; superseded process allowed emailing any employee. Tests whether system surfaces the outdated intake path.

items.question: How long do we have to respond to a subject access request in the UK?
How many days does a US consumer privacy request response have under our policy?
How long does it take to respond to a privacy request?
items.notes: DE/UK say 1 month (extendable), US says 45 days — different enough that a single silent answer would be misleading. Should clarify or summarise both.

items.question: What is our policy on remote work stipends?
items.notes: No policy area in the corpus covers this at all. Tests whether the system refuses cleanly rather than retrieving the nearest tangentially-related document (e.g. expense policy) and answering from it anyway.

items.question: Since German enterprise refund terms changed in 2025, does that also mean the German SMB refund terms changed?
items.notes: Tests whether the system incorrectly assumes changes to one segment's policy apply to the other segment, versus correctly checking both documents and reporting the SMB policy is a separate, unaffected document.

items.question: Our German enterprise contract predates 2025 — does the old 30-day refund window still apply to us?
items.notes: Genuinely nuanced: the current policy applies to invoices dated on/after 1 Jan 2025, but doesn't say existing contracts are grandfathered. Correct answer should flag this ambiguity rather than confidently asserting either way — counts as correct if it surfaces both documents and the ambiguity.

items.question: Do California employees get PTO payout at termination?
items.notes: Tests retrieval of a specific clause (California carve-out) embedded within a broader US document, not just document-level matching.

items.question: What VAT threshold triggers the receipt requirement for German expense claims?
